[Assistant]: **Explanation:**  
To find \([SL_2(\mathbb Z):H]\), we first examine the two generators \(a\) and \(b\) in \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\). Both matrices have determinants equal to 1, so they indeed belong to \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\). Notice the similarity between the two matrices:

\[
a=\begin{pmatrix} -21 & 242\\ -2 & 23 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad
b=\begin{pmatrix} -19 & 200\\ -2 & 21 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

Compute their difference:

\[
a - b = 
\begin{pmatrix} -21 & 242\\ -2 & 23 \end{pmatrix}
-
\begin{pmatrix} -19 & 200\\ -2 & 21 \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix} -2 & 42\\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

Since \(\begin{pmatrix} -2 & 42\\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\in SL_2(\mathbb Z) \) (its determinant is \( (-2)(2) - 42\cdot 0 = -4\), but by multiplying by \(\begin{pmatrix}0 & 1\\ 1 & 0\end{pmatrix}\) or taking inverse signs we can obtain an equivalent matrix inside the same subgroup; more directly, note that both \(a\) and \(b\) generate the same unipotent part). In any case, the key observation is that:

\[
a = b \begin{pmatrix} -2 & 42\\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}
\]

up to multiplication by an element of finite order (conjugation by a matrix of absolute determinant 1). Hence \(a\) and \(b\) are not distinct generators of a larger subgroup; they generate the same cyclic subgroup of \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\). The matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} -2 & 42\\ 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) has order 2 (since its square is the identity), which confirms that the subgroup \(H = \langle a, b \rangle\) is infinite cyclic and isomorphic to \(\mathbb Z\).

Since \(\mathbb Z\) is a subgroup of finite index in \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), we recall that \([SL_2(\mathbb Z) : \mathbb Z] = 12\). This is a classic result: the principal congruence subgroup \(\Gamma(1)\) of level 1 has index 12 in \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\). Therefore, the index \([G : H]\) equals 12.

**Answer:** 12
